text.p: Swiss retail group Jelmoli said it expects a net profit in the area of 50 million to 60 million Swiss francs in the business years 1997 and 1998 after bouncing back in 1996 from a loss in 1995.
Jelmoli also said it expected annual dividends to be between 30 and 35 Swiss francs per share on the 1997 and 1998 results.
"If consumer demand accelerates, profits could also increase more," the company said in a statement.
Jelmoli reported 1996 net profit after minority interests of 45.1 million Swiss francs following a loss of 13.4 million the year before.
After paying no dividend on 1995's loss, Jelmoli proposed a dividend of 28 francs per bearer share and 5.60 francs per registered share on 1996 results.
The 1995 loss was largely due to major restructuring that shed most of its loss-making department stores and trimmed its mail order business.

Jelmoli's statement said its strongest performing businesses, Swiss home electronics chain Dipl. Ing. Fust AG and real estate manager Immobilian, would support profit growth with annual operating results of 30 million to 40 million Swiss francs each.

Jelmoli Holding's other main businesses are department store and mail-order group Jelmoli AG, travel agent chain Imholz Reisen AG, U.S. subsidiary Appleseed's Inc, eyewear chain Kochoptik AG and dry cleaners Terlinden-jelmoli Reinigungen AG.
